questions.question: Q57. The Master Budget for an entire organization:
options: Is used only for external reporting to shareholders and investors
Brings together the departmental or activity budgets for all departments and responsibility centers within the organization
Is prepared exclusively by the finance director
Contains only the sales and production budgets
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q58. If the budgeted profit, cash position, or balance sheet are unsatisfactory:
options: The budgets should be submitted to the board without any changes
The budgets should be revised until a satisfactory planned outcome is achieved
The organization should seek external funding to bridge the gap
The organization must immediately reduce its workforce
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q59. Regarding the level of difficulty in budget preparation, budgets should be:
options: Realistic and just tough enough — not so difficult as to demotivate, not so easy as to present a lack of motivation
Very easy to achieve to maintain high morale and satisfaction
Set exclusively by senior management without employee input
Extremely challenging to maximize employee motivation
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q60. The risk of allowing managers to have input into budgets for which they are also responsible is:
options: Managers may build slack into budgets — setting targets below what is achievable
Managers will ignore the budget once it has been approved
Managers will set overly ambitious targets to impress senior management
Managers will refuse to participate in the budgeting process
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q61. The link between budgets and organizational objectives is important because:
options: Budgets should be independent of strategic objectives to maintain flexibility
Budgets linked to objectives motivate managers and staff to achieve those objectives rather than pursuing their own personal goals
Objectives are always financial and therefore automatically align with budgets
Budgets replace the need for strategic objectives in operational planning
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q62. Revenue per Employee as an efficiency ratio is calculated as:
options: Sales / Number of Employees
Gross Profit / Number of Employees EM MCQ BANK
Net Profit / Number of Employees
Operating Profit / Number of Employees
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q63. Dividend Cover is calculated as:
options: Share Price / EPS
PBIT / Interest
Debt / Equity
PAT / Total Dividend
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q64. Payables Days is calculated as:
options: Receivables Balance / Credit Sales × 365
Payable Balance / Credit Purchases × 365
Inventory / Cost of Sales × 365
Current Assets / Current Liabilities
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q65. Which of the following best describes the purpose of a Budgeted Income Statement as part of the Master Budget?
options: It coordinates the production and sales budgets into a unified plan
It communicates strategic objectives to all organizational levels
It authorizes departmental expenditure for the coming period
It summarizes the expected revenues and costs to show the planned profit for the budget period
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q1. The performance measurement mix is described as an essential part of:
options: The human resource planning and recruitment process
The strategic control process — the ability to measure output in terms of the objectives
The financial budgeting and annual planning process
The marketing strategy and brand management process
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q2. The bus company illustration in Chapter 13 demonstrates that:
options: Employee bonuses should be based only on financial metrics
Linking bonuses to simple performance measures always improves output
Performance measures should be set exclusively by senior management
Poorly designed performance measures lead to sub-optimal behaviour — drivers skipped stops to meet the on-time KPI
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q3. The challenge in designing a performance measurement system is to:
options: Delegate all measurement responsibilities to the finance department
Use only financial measures to ensure comparability
Maximize the number of measures to cover all possible outcomes
Design a measurement mix that can be used in the control process without proving to be a burden or confusing
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q4. Setting performance measures is important for which TWO key reasons?
options: Complying with government regulations and satisfying external auditors
Reducing production costs and maximizing shareholder returns
Management must identify whether the strategy has the desired effect AND setting measures communicates targets and priorities to staff
Attracting new customers and improving brand awareness
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q5. Which of the following is an example of a poorly designed performance measure for a hospital?
options: Focusing on waiting times for patients — which may lead to rushing procedures and sending patients home too early, harming quality
Measuring inventory turnover and carbon footprint reduction
Monitoring the number of defective products produced
Tracking customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rates
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q6. When a measure is added to the performance measurement system, what message does this send to staff?
options: The importance of that item is being highlighted and it is now a priority
The measure is being tested and may be removed in the future
The organization is complying with new government regulations
That item is no longer important to the organization EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 107 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q7. When a measure is DROPPED from the performance measurement system, management must be aware that:
options: Staff will immediately improve performance in that area
It communicates to staff that this item is no longer important — management must decide if that is the intended message
The measure will be replaced by an equivalent external benchmark
Financial costs will automatically decrease
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q8. Too many changes to the performance measurement system can result in:
options: Automatic improvement in all performance dimensions simultaneously
Improved strategic alignment and clearer employee focus
Reduced operational costs and improved efficiency
Indicator overload — confusing employees about what the organization wants them to achieve
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q9. Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of Financial Measures of Performance?
options: They provide a wider view beyond just financial metrics
They have positive motivational implications for non-financial staff
They are not distorted by inflation
They can be easily compared across companies — providing insights into relative financial health
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q10. "Leads to suboptimal and short-term behaviour" is a DISADVANTAGE of which type of performance measure?
options: Non-financial measures
Qualitative performance indicators
Financial measures — focusing solely on financial metrics may encourage short-term decision-making at the expense of long-term sustainability
Multidimensional performance models
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q11. Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of Financial Measures related to cost?
options: They require specialist training for all employees to understand
They are costlier to implement than non-financial measures
It is relatively inexpensive to gather and analyze financial data compared to some non- financial measures
They require extensive IT infrastructure to collect and process
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q12. "Understood by the select few" is a DISADVANTAGE of:
options: Financial measures — they may be complex and understood only by those with financial expertise
Performance pyramid measures — too hierarchical for service firms EM MCQ BANK
Non-financial measures — too complex for financial experts
Balanced scorecard measures — too broad for operational use
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q13. "Subjectivity can exist in calculation" as a disadvantage of financial measures refers to:
options: Managers manipulating non-financial data to improve reported performance
Certain financial measures such as depreciation involving subjective judgments that impact accuracy
Government regulators imposing different accounting standards
External auditors disagreeing with internal performance assessments
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q14. Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of Non-Financial Measures?
options: They are understood exclusively by financial experts
They are always cheap and easy to implement
They are never subject to inflation distortion — providing a more accurate representation of performance
They are always comparable across different companies and industries
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q15. "Can emphasize broad spectrum of management" is an advantage of non-financial measures because:
options: They are always cheaper to implement than financial measures
They eliminate the need for financial ratio analysis
They can highlight aspects of performance related to customer satisfaction, employee engagement, and innovation — beyond financial metrics
They reduce the number of performance indicators required
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q16. "Culture clash implications" is a disadvantage of non-financial measures because:
options: Non-financial measures always conflict with government regulations
Non-financial measures are too expensive for small organizations
Non-financial measures require too much IT infrastructure to implement
Non-financial measures may clash with the existing organizational culture or management practices, leading to resistance or confusion
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q17. "Constant change requires constant monitoring" as a disadvantage of non-financial measures refers to:
options: Non-financial measures being distorted by inflation over time
Non-financial measures being too stable and not reflecting business changes
Non-financial measures requiring government approval before implementation
Non-financial measures needing to be regularly updated or modified to remain relevant — requiring ongoing monitoring and adjustment
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q18. Which of the following correctly summarizes a key difference between financial and non- financial measures?
options: Financial measures are always better than non-financial measures for strategic decision making EM MCQ BANK
Financial measures are never subjective; non-financial measures are always objective
Financial measures tend to focus on resource generation and survival long-term; non- financial measures provide a wider view and can motivate positively
Non-financial measures are always cheaper and easier than financial measures
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q19. Fitzgerald and Moon's Building Block Model was adopted as a framework for:
options: Recruiting and developing high-performing employees
Setting annual financial budgets and sales targets
The design and analysis of performance management systems
Designing marketing campaigns and brand strategies
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q20. The three building blocks in Fitzgerald and Moon's model are:
options: Dimensions, Standards, and Rewards
Planning, Controlling, and Reporting
Objectives, Strategies, and Tactics
Financial, Non-financial, and Qualitative measures
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q21. "Dimensions" in Fitzgerald and Moon's Building Block Model refer to:
options: The financial ratios used to assess organizational profitability
The rewards given to employees who exceed performance targets
The standards used to measure employee compliance
The goals for the business — suitable measures must be developed for each performance dimension
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q22. How many dimensions are identified in Fitzgerald and Moon's Building Block Model?
options: Five
Four
Seven
Six
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q23. Which of the following is NOT one of the six dimensions in Fitzgerald and Moon's Building Block Model?
options: Financial Performance
Competitiveness
Innovation
Cost Leadership
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q24. "Competitiveness" as a dimension in Fitzgerald and Moon's model refers to:
options: The drive and capacity to introduce new ideas, processes, or products
How efficiently a company utilizes its available resources
The ability of the company to stand out and perform better than its competitors
The level of excellence in delivering services to customers
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q25. "Resource Utilization" as a dimension in Fitzgerald and Moon's model refers to:
options: The ability to outperform competitors in the market
The capacity to adapt and change as per the market or customer needs
How efficiently a company utilizes its available resources
The level of excellence in delivering services to customers
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q26. "Standards" in Fitzgerald and Moon's Building Block Model must satisfy which criterion related to "Ownership"?
options: Standards must be identical across all departments and divisions
Standards must be set exclusively by senior management
Standards must be set by external auditors to ensure objectivity EM MCQ BANK
Standards must involve managers in the setting process — promoting acceptance and motivation
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q27. "Achievability" as a criterion for setting Standards in the Building Block Model means:
options: Standards must be set below what the organization can realistically achieve
Goals must be achieved within a single financial quarter
Goals must be tough but possible — so they motivate instead of discourage
Standards must be set by external benchmarking against industry leaders
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q28. "Fairness" as a criterion for setting Standards in the Building Block Model means:
options: All employees receive identical rewards regardless of performance
Standards are reviewed annually by an independent external body
Standards are equitably set across the organization — ensuring no department or individual faces undue pressure
Standards are set based solely on financial metrics to eliminate subjectivity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q29. "Clarity" as a criterion for setting Rewards in Fitzgerald and Moon's model means:
options: Rewards are set exclusively by the finance department
Rewards are only given to senior management who achieve strategic targets
Rewards are automatically linked to financial performance metrics only
Rewards are transparent and understood by all — what is being rewarded and why
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q30. "Link to Standards" as a criterion for setting Rewards means:
options: Rewards are set by government regulations and cannot be modified
Rewards are directly tied to performance standards — ensuring a clear line of sight between effort and reward
Rewards are decided at the end of the year regardless of performance
Rewards are linked only to financial results and shareholder returns
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q31. "Desirability" as a criterion for setting Rewards in the Building Block Model means:
options: Rewards must be approved by the board before being communicated to employees
Rewards must always be financial in nature such as bonuses and pay rises
Rewards must be identical for all employees to ensure fairness
Rewards offered are genuinely sought after by employees — be it monetary, recognition, or growth opportunities
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q32. The Balanced Scorecard was presented by:
options: Fitzgerald and Moon in 1989
Lynch and Cross in 1991
Porter and Miles in 1994
Kaplan and Norton in 1992
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q33. The Balanced Scorecard is described as:
options: A financial reporting tool designed exclusively for external stakeholders

An approach to providing information to management to assist strategic policy formulation — emphasizing a set of information addressing all relevant performance issues in an objective and unbiased fashion
A budgetary control system for managing departmental expenditure EM MCQ BANK
A marketing strategy framework for analyzing competitive advantage
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q34. The Balanced Scorecard was developed as a response to traditional performance measurement which had:
options: Required excessive data collection that resulted in indicator overload
Focused too broadly on non-financial measures at the expense of profitability
Placed too much emphasis on customer satisfaction and employee engagement
Tended to focus on a narrow range of performance measures and adopted a short- term focus
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q35. Kaplan likened running a business to flying a plane because:
options: Both are simple enough to manage with just financial indicators
Just as a pilot needs multiple instruments such as airspeed, altitude, and fuel level, business managers need a broad set of indicators beyond just financial metrics
Both require identical information systems to be effective
Both require a single key metric to guide decision making
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q36. The four perspectives of the Balanced Scorecard are:
options: Competitiveness, Financial Performance, Quality, and Innovation
Strategy, Operations, Marketing, and HR
Planning, Controlling, Coordinating, and Communicating
Financial, Customer, Internal Business Processes, and Learning and Growth
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q37. The Financial Perspective of the Balanced Scorecard focuses on:
options: How well the organization is meeting its monetary goals — such as making profits and generating revenue
The internal systems and processes that drive performance
How the organization delivers value to its customers
How employees are developed and innovation is encouraged
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q38. The Customer Perspective of the Balanced Scorecard focuses on:
options: Monitoring financial ratios and profitability metrics
Enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty — measuring how well the organization delivers value to customers
Developing employee skills and fostering a culture of innovation
Improving internal systems and operational efficiency
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q39. The Internal Business Processes Perspective of the Balanced Scorecard focuses on:
options: Building customer relationships and improving satisfaction scores
Developing employee capabilities and encouraging innovation
Improving supply chain efficiency, operational processes, and internal systems
Meeting financial targets and shareholder expectations
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q40. The Learning and Growth Perspective of the Balanced Scorecard focuses on:
options: Optimizing internal processes and reducing operational waste
Fostering employee development, innovation, and organizational learning
Maximizing revenue and profit margins
Improving customer satisfaction and market share
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q41. In the Green Mart Balanced Scorecard example, the Financial Perspective target includes: EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 112 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Increasing employee training hours by 25%
Maintaining a customer satisfaction rating of at least 4 out of 5
Increasing inventory turnover by 20% and reducing carbon emissions by 15%
Achieving a 10% increase in sales revenue and maintaining a net profit margin of 8%
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q42. In the Green Mart Balanced Scorecard example, the Internal Business Processes Perspective measures include:
options: Employee training hours and number of new product ideas
Total sales revenue and net profit margin
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rate
Inventory turnover rate and carbon footprint reduction
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q43. "Strategy Mapping" was developed by Kaplan and Norton as:
options: A replacement for the Balanced Scorecard in complex organizations
A financial analysis technique for comparing departmental budgets
A standalone strategic planning tool independent of the Balanced Scorecard
An extension to the Balanced Scorecard to make implementations more successful — showing cause-and-effect relationships between objectives
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q44. A key problem with the Balanced Scorecard identified in the chapter is that:
options: Many employees do not understand the organization's strategy and systems such as performance management are not linked to the strategy
It requires too many external benchmarks to be effective
It focuses too heavily on non-financial measures at the expense of profitability
It is only applicable to manufacturing organizations and not service firms
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q45. The Balanced Scorecard helps reduce the tendency to:
options: Align internal processes with external customer requirements
Concentrate on one measure — broadening the manager's view of performance
Focus on a broad range of measures simultaneously
Develop long-term strategic objectives for the organization
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q46. Gains in one Balanced Scorecard perspective need to be considered alongside:
options: Only the customer perspective to maintain competitive advantage
Government regulations and compliance requirements
Losses that may arise in other perspectives — encouraging a holistic view
Only the financial perspective regardless of other outcomes
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q47. The main reason for the creation of Multidimensional Performance Models is:
options: Government regulations now require multidimensional reporting from all organizations

Traditional financial performance systems have moved from being a performance system more to an information system aimed at satisfying external stakeholders — poorly designed to guide organizational direction EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 113 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
Non-financial measures have proven to be more accurate than financial measures
Financial measures have become too complex for managers to understand
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q48. A key criticism of traditional performance systems is that managers have learned to:
options: Set overly ambitious targets to attract investor interest
Ignore financial targets and focus on non-financial outcomes
Rely entirely on external benchmarks rather than internal performance data
Manage the traditional performance systems to obtain numbers that meet goals and secure bonuses — rather than managing the business itself
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q49. Advances in technology have paradoxically created which problem for performance measurement?
options: Reduced data collection capabilities across organizations
An overload of information — vital information gets lost among excessive data
Inability to process complex financial calculations in real time
Reduced accuracy in financial reporting and ratio analysis
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q50. Service businesses face a fundamental challenge in measuring performance because:
options: Their production processes are identical to manufacturing firms
They have no financial costs that need to be measured or controlled
Their customers, activities, and deals vary too widely — and people bring unpredictable differences in experience, skills, and motivation
They are prohibited from using external benchmarks for comparison
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q51. The FIRST principle of service measurement states that service companies should:
options: Outsource all measurement activities to specialist consultancies
Compare themselves against their own performance — rather than against poorly defined external measures
Focus primarily on comparing against external industry benchmarks
Use only financial costs to measure performance variance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q52. The SECOND principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Focus only on top-level financial costs to keep analysis simple
Look deeper than their financial costs to discover and monitor the root causes of those expenses
Restrict measurement to quantitative metrics and avoid qualitative data
Compare their performance against the top three competitors in their industry
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q53. The THIRD principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Replace all internal measurement with external benchmarking
Restrict measurement to a single functional area to avoid complexity
Set up broad cost-measurement systems to report and compare all expenses across functional silos — improving understanding of cross-functional trade-offs
Focus all measurement on individual employee productivity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q54. Why is variance particularly difficult to measure in service businesses? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 114 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Service activities are identical across all locations making comparison unnecessary
Service businesses are not required to measure performance by law
Service businesses are too small to afford sophisticated measurement systems
Metrics are not uniform across business units — for example one group in a call center may regard all calls on a given issue as a single case while another logs every call separately
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q55. "Service-level agreements" create measurement challenges because:
options: The more types of services a business offers, the more variability it can expect in its agreements
They eliminate the need for performance measurement in service firms
They require only financial metrics to assess compliance
They are always identical across all customer types and service lines
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q56. "Internal benchmarks" are recommended over "external benchmarks" for service companies because:
options: Internal benchmarks deliver more detailed metrics — allowing a company to find its own best practices and understand true cost drivers with full access to relevant information
External benchmarks always lead to overestimation of performance variance
Government regulations prohibit the use of external benchmarks in service firms
External benchmarks are always more accurate than internal data
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q57. A "Cost Tree with Detailed Metrics" is described as:
options: A government-required reporting format for service companies
A financial statement showing total organizational expenditure
A marketing tool for analyzing the profitability of different customer segments

An important tool to help companies define internal benchmarks — allowing managers to compare performance of different accounts against similar metrics and calculate which improvements will have the most impact
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q58. "Measure Cost Drivers" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Measuring only the top-level financial costs of service delivery
Looking at the underlying cause of each expense — such as cost per employee, incidents per employee per day, or incidents per product — rather than just the total cost
Comparing service costs against the industry average benchmark
Outsourcing all cost analysis to specialist financial consultants
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q59. "Measure Deep and Broad" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Using only external benchmarks to ensure objectivity
Taking a comprehensive approach — measuring all relevant costs rather than only selected costs — because services are fungible and it is easy to shift costs to unmeasured areas
Focusing measurement on a single key cost area to maximize precision
Restricting measurement to financial costs only
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q60. The Performance Pyramid was developed by:
options: Porter and Miles as an extension of the competitive strategy framework
Kaplan and Norton in 1992
Lynch and Cross as a model to understand and define the links between objectives and performance measures at different levels in the organization
Fitzgerald and Moon in the 1990s
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q61. The Performance Pyramid is designed to ensure that:
options: Financial measures take precedence over non-financial measures at all levels
Only senior management is responsible for setting performance targets
The activities of every department, system, and business unit support the overall vision of the organization
Performance measurement is restricted to the top two levels of the organization
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q62. At the TOP of the Performance Pyramid is:
options: Business operating system measures of internal processes
The Vision — through which the organization describes how it will achieve long-term success and competitive advantage
Day-to-day operational measures
Business unit critical success factors in terms of market and financial measures
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q63. The SECOND level of the Performance Pyramid — the Business Unit — includes:
options: Internal systems and processes needed to meet customer needs
The overall vision and long-term competitive strategy
Critical success factors in terms of market-related measures and financial measures
Day-to-day operational measures of productivity and quality
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q64. The THIRD level of the Performance Pyramid — Business Operating Systems — includes:
options: Critical success factors in terms of market share and financial returns
The overall organizational vision and mission
Day-to-day operational measures at the shop-floor level
Measures relating to internal systems and processes needed to meet the needs of customers — such as flexibility measures showing responsiveness to customer demands
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q65. The LOWEST level of the Performance Pyramid contains:
options: Business unit critical success factors and financial targets
Day-to-day operational measures
Internal process measures and operational flexibility metrics
The organizational vision and long-term competitive strategy
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q66. In the Performance Pyramid, objectives flow in which direction?
options: From the left side of the pyramid to the right side
From the bottom of the pyramid upward to the vision
Downward — cascading from the vision through to operational measures
In both directions simultaneously at all levels
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q67. In the Performance Pyramid, measures and information flow in which direction? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 116 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: From the bottom upward — operational measures inform higher-level performance
From right to left — from financial to non-financial
Downward from the vision to operational measures
From the left side to the right side at each level
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q68. The LEFT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Strategic-level measures linked only to shareholder returns
Predominantly financial and internally focused
Day-to-day operational measures only
Predominantly non-financial and externally focused
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q69. The RIGHT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Externally focused and non-financial
Related to customer satisfaction and market share
Related to innovation and employee development
Focused on the internal efficiency of the organization and predominantly financial
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q70. A limitation of the Performance Pyramid identified in the chapter is that it:
options: Focuses too heavily on financial measures at all levels
Tends to concentrate on only two groups of stakeholders — shareholders and customers — making it necessary to ensure measures for other stakeholders are also included
Does not include any non-financial measures of performance
Is too complex and hierarchical for practical implementation in service firms
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Q71. CIMA's official definition of Performance Measurement describes it as:
options: A financial reporting tool for satisfying external stakeholder requirements
A marketing tool for measuring customer satisfaction and brand equity
A human resource tool for evaluating individual employee performance
The process of assessing the proficiency with which a reporting entity succeeds — by the economic acquisition of resources and their efficient and effective deployment — in achieving its objectives
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q72. Which of the following is identified as a reason why setting performance measures is "often more difficult than would first be imagined"?
options: Performance measures are too expensive for small organizations to implement
Government regulations restrict the types of measures organizations can use
Improving one objective — such as hospital waiting times — can have a negative effect on another equally important objective — such as quality of healthcare
Employees always resist the introduction of new performance measurement systems
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q73. The link between CSFs and performance measurement ensures that:
options: The performance measurement system ties into the overall strategy — areas where results must be satisfactory for competitive success are measured and monitored EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 117 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
All departments use identical performance measures regardless of strategic priorities
Only financial CSFs are translated into measurable KPIs
Performance measures are set exclusively by external consultants
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q74. KPIs for the CSF of "efficient production" in a cost leadership strategy could include:
options: Employee engagement levels and training hours
Market share growth and brand awareness scores
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rates
Maximum kg of materials wasted and average time taken to produce one unit
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q75. Once a performance measurement system is implemented, management must ensure that:
options: The system remains identical regardless of changes in the business environment
Only senior management has access to performance data
Performance measures are reviewed only at the annual board meeting
Information systems are put in place to collect data allowing performance to be measured on an ongoing basis
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Q76. Which of the following correctly identifies the FOUR perspectives of the Balanced Scorecard with an appropriate example measure?
options: Financial — total sales revenue; Customer — customer satisfaction scores; Internal — inventory turnover rate; Learning — employee training hours
Financial — market share; Customer — carbon footprint; Internal — revenue growth; Learning — repeat purchase rate
Financial — customer loyalty; Customer — profit margin; Internal — training hours; Learning — stock price
Financial — employee training hours; Customer — net profit margin; Internal — customer satisfaction; Learning — inventory turnover
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q77. Which building block of Fitzgerald and Moon's model ensures employees are motivated to achieve standards?
options: Rewards — by linking clear and desirable incentives to standard achievement
Standards — by setting achievable and fair benchmarks
All three building blocks equally — no single block is more important
Dimensions — by providing clear goals for the business
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q78. Which of the following BEST explains why multidimensional performance models were created?
options: Technology limitations prevented accurate financial data collection
Traditional financial systems were too expensive to maintain

Traditional financial systems were designed primarily to satisfy external stakeholders and poorly designed to guide internal organizational direction — while managers learned to manage the numbers rather than the business
Government regulations required organizations to adopt non-financial reporting
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Q79. In CIMA's terminology, "economic acquisition of resources" as part of performance measurement refers to:
options: Acquiring resources at minimum cost — the efficiency of resource procurement
Eliminating all non-essential resources from the production process EM MCQ BANK
Maximizing production output regardless of resource cost
Purchasing resources exclusively from domestic suppliers
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Q80. Which of the following statements about the Balanced Scorecard is TRUE?
options: It focuses exclusively on internal operational efficiency
It was designed to replace all existing financial performance measures
It is only applicable to large multinational corporations with complex operations
It brings together a wide range of financial and non-financial measures to give managers a broader perspective — ensuring gains in one area are considered alongside losses in other areas
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D
